survey-analysis.name: Survey Analysis
survey-analysis.summary: Structured walk-through of survey results: topic, executive summary, methodology, findings, analysis, implications, recommendations. Built so a reader who only sees the second slide already knows the headline insight.

beats.name: Introduction
beats.description: Open by naming the question the survey was meant to answer. Why this, why now, who commissioned it. Anchor the audience in the decision the survey is designed to inform.

beats.name: Executive Summary
beats.description: State the top three findings in plain language on a single slide. A reader who only sees this slide should still be able to make the right call. Avoid hedging — synthesis is the point.

beats.name: Context
beats.description: Detail the situation behind the survey: prior knowledge, related research, the gap this work fills. Just enough to position the findings as new information rather than restated common sense.

beats.name: Data & Methodology
beats.description: Describe how the data was collected and from whom. Sample size, recruitment, instrument, timing. Be honest about limitations; methodological transparency is what gives the findings their weight.

beats.name: Data Summary
beats.description: Give the audience an overview of the dataset before drilling in. Demographics, response rates, distribution of key variables. Help them calibrate what 'most' and 'few' mean in this study.

beats.name: Findings
beats.description: Present the key insights one at a time. Lead each finding with the claim, then the chart. Avoid burying the point under the visualization — captions should restate the insight in words.

beats.name: Data Analysis
beats.description: Break down the data behind each finding: cross-tabs, segment splits, statistical confidence. This is the slide skeptics will scrutinize — make it scrutinizable.

beats.name: Implications
beats.description: Translate findings into 'so what.' What changes for product, marketing, ops, the customer? Implications without consequences are interesting trivia, not research.

beats.name: Recommendations
beats.description: Provide the actions that follow from the implications. Prioritize, attach owners, mark which require decisions. This is where research becomes useful.

beats.name: Conclusion
beats.description: Recap the headline finding and the most important recommendation. End with the next step — a follow-on study, a workshop, a decision — so the work doesn't sit on a shelf.

investor.name: Investor
investor.summary: Angel investors, VCs, or institutional investors evaluating financial viability, market opportunity, and team.
investor.description: Angel, venture, and institutional investors judging financial viability, market opportunity, and the team. Lead with traction, size the market (TAM, SAM, SOM), make the moat and differentiation explicit, and show financial projections with their assumptions stated. Moderate chart density; 12-20 slides.

pitch.name: Pitch
pitch.summary: Present an opportunity and ask for investment, approval, partnership, or sponsorship.
pitch.description: Use when the deck needs to create interest and move a high-stakes audience toward backing the opportunity. Lead with the opportunity, prove credibility, and make the ask concrete.
pitch.outcome: The audience agrees to invest, sponsor, approve, or continue the conversation.
successCriteria: Ask and next step are explicit

technical.name: Technical
technical.summary: Precise, evidence-led voice for engineering, research, and product-detail audiences.
technical.description: Lead with the question or claim, then walk through the mechanism and the numbers. Use exact terminology; assume the audience can handle and prefers it. Diagrams, tables, and benchmarks are first-class.
voiceCues: State the claim, then the mechanism, then the evidence.
Use exact terminology — don't soften technical terms for general readability.
Quote benchmarks with conditions (cold/warm, p50/p95/p99, dataset, hardware).
Prefer diagrams and tables over prose paragraphs for structural information.
samplePhrases: p95 inference latency is 38ms on a single A100, down from 312ms on the prior runtime.
We replaced the streaming serializer with a batched protobuf path; throughput rose 4.2× under load.
The result holds for context windows up to 32k tokens; beyond that, see appendix B.

classic.name: Classic
classic.description: A timeless, clean, and versatile theme with balanced color contrasts and classic typography. Ideal for professional, readable presentations.

vibes.name: Vibes
vibes.summary: Expressive purple, green, and orange accents for creative decks.
vibes.description: A vibrant mixed-accent scheme for presentations that need personality, motion, and visual variety.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

lucida-sans.name: Lucida Sans
lucida-sans.description: Lucida Sans is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Lucida Sans for both headings and body text.

tenorite.name: Tenorite
tenorite.description: Tenorite is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Tenorite Display for headings with Tenorite for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
